phase: /private/var becomes the HFS+ volume on the flash, and keeps its contents across a reboot

what_changed.the_mechanism_was_already_there: init.c:834 mount_data_volume() reads a var_hfs= boot argument, mounts that device on /private/var, and falls back to ramfs when it cannot
two_edits: coordinator/loader-build.json: -DXNU_EXTRA_ARGS gained var_hfs=xnusys_var (XNU_EXTRA_ARGS has an #ifndef guard, so no source change was needed)

why_the_vm_directory_had_to_go.the_constants: vm_compressor_backing_store.h: for !XNU_TARGET_OS_OSX, MIN_SWAP_FILE_SIZE is 64 MiB and MAX_SWAP_FILE_SIZE is 128 MiB (the 1 GiB figure belongs to the OSX branch)
why_the_vm_directory_had_to_go.what_would_happen: the volume is 174 MiB with 162 MiB free, so a 128 MiB swapfile fits on the first try and would take 79% of it
why_the_vm_directory_had_to_go.what_was_measured: freeBlocks went 41440 -> 39217, i.e. 2223 blocks = 8.7 MiB, which is the size of the skeleton plus what launchd wrote. A swapfile would have shown 32768 blocks.

how_the_mechanism_works.on_failure: prints 'HFS Plus from %s: %s; a memory filesystem instead, empty at every boot' and falls back to ramfs, so a broken volume cannot stop the boot
after_mounting: empty_tree on /private/var/tmp, /run and /vm, so those three are each boot's own
read /etc/var.skel and create 110 directories, 2 symlinks and 8 files with their modes and owners
write three .migrated markers so logd treats the log directories as new
how_the_mechanism_works.where_the_skeleton_files_come_from: in_image() prefixes /redwood, so the eight plists are read from the read-only system image, not from the memory disk's /var -- which is why turning /var into a symlink cannot break the copy

measurements.read_of_the_file_count: 765 after 793a and 765 after 793b: everything the first boot created survived the restart

793a.design: boot with var_hfs=xnusys_var, let init mount /private/var, run launchd.ios, no unmount
kernel_log: /private/var: HFS Plus from /dev/xnusys_var, kept between boots
793a.swapfile: no vm_swap_create_file failure and no 128 MiB allocation; freeBlocks fell by 8.7 MiB instead
793a.launchd: ran to the loader's 440-second return, 60 frames a second, same as the memory-disk baseline

793b.design: same image, nothing written to the flash, just reboot onto the dirty volume
793b.mount: /private/var: HFS Plus from /dev/xnusys_var, kept between boots -- it mounted a volume that was never unmounted
793b.no_replay_journal_line: because 793a's fsync had already checkpointed the journal (start == end); there was nothing uncommitted to replay. That it mounted at all in the Unmounted=0 state is the journal working: without one the volume refuses a writable mount
793b.data: fileCount 765 -> 765, so the skeleton, the eight plists and everything launchd wrote in 793a all came back

still_open_var_is_not_a_symlink.meaning: system services write to /var/root/..., and /var is still the memory disk's own directory (drwxr-xr-x /redwood/var), so that data is lost every boot
still_open_var_is_not_a_symlink.so: /private/var/* survives a reboot and /var/* does not
still_open_var_is_not_a_symlink.fix: standard iOS has /var -> private/var. var.skel has no such entry. The obstacle is that /var already exists as a non-empty directory, so symlink() returns EEXIST and it has to be removed first.

how_it_was_verified.var_hfs_reached_the_kernel: strings loader-out/loader.bin shows the whole command line ending in '... ufs=2 var_hfs=xnusys_var loader_return_after=420'
how_it_was_verified.the_volume_is_in_use: fileCount 9 -> 765 and, after the second boot, folderCount 4980; this is not a volume that mounted and sat idle
